text: Which field studies animal behavior in its natural and evolutionary context?
A question about how hormones trigger a bird's song asks for which kind of explanation?
A question about why birdsong increased mating success asks for which kind of explanation?
A duckling follows the first moving adult it sees soon after hatching. Which learning process is this?
An animal gradually ignores a harmless repeated sound. Which learning process is this?
A repeated mild stimulus produces a stronger, rather than weaker, response. What is this?
A dog learns to expect food when a bell rings after repeated pairings. This is what?
A rat presses a lever more often after receiving food for doing so. This is what?
A behavior becomes less frequent after its reward stops arriving. This is called what?
An insect moves directly toward a light source. What orientation behavior is this?
A bacterium moves toward a nutrient chemical. What orientation behavior is this?
Movement with direction set by a stimulus is called what?
Movement whose speed changes with stimulus intensity but lacks a set direction is what?
A response automatically triggered by a specific stimulus, without prior learning, is what?
A stereotyped sequence that runs after a triggering cue is a what?
The specific cue that releases a stereotyped behavior is called a what?
A roughly 24-hour internal cycle of activity is a what?
A regular seasonal journey between breeding and wintering grounds is what?
The ability to return to a particular nest site after traveling is called what?
Moving away from one's birthplace to establish elsewhere is called what?
An animal defending an area against rivals shows what behavior?
A ritualized display used to attract a mate is part of what?
Traits favored because they improve mating success reflect what process?
A peacock's tail can be favored by mate choice despite survival costs. Which process?
Selection driven by competition among members of one sex for mates is what?
Selection driven by mate choice between sexes is what?
A marked difference in form between males and females of a species is called what?
A group of males displaying at a shared site while females choose among them is a what?
One male mating with several females describes which mating system?
One female mating with several males describes which mating system?
A pair bond between one male and one female describes which mating system?
An animal that sacrifices resources to help a relative may increase what total fitness measure?
Evolutionary favoring of helping genetically related individuals is called what?
The genetic relatedness of full siblings is approximately what fraction?
A worker bee forgoes reproduction while helping raise relatives. Which social system is this?
Cooperative brood care and reproductive division of labor are hallmarks of what?
Distinct worker and reproductive roles in an insect colony are called what?
A chemical signal released by one animal and detected by another of its species is a what?
Bees use a movement display to communicate food direction and distance. What is it called?
A vocalization that warns nearby group members of danger is called what?
A conspicuous display that signals strength and may avert fighting is a what?
A stable ranking among group members for access to resources is a what?
Which predator-avoidance tactic relies on matching the background?
Bright coloring that advertises a genuine defense to predators is what?
A harmless species resembling a defended species shows what kind of mimicry?
Two defended species converging on the same warning pattern show what kind of mimicry?
A predator resembling a harmless object to lure prey shows which broad strategy?
A forager balancing food gain against time and risk illustrates what theory?
When many eyes scan for predators, group living can improve what?
A whale calling across long ocean distances uses which communication channel?
Ants following a deposited scent trail use which communication channel?
A firefly's flashes to attract a mate use which communication channel?
An animal's daily activity shifting in response to light cues is a form of what?
For a migrating bird, Earth's magnetic field can serve as what?
An animal learns a route by forming a representation of landmarks. What is that representation?
A juvenile learns a species-specific song from adults. Which broad category of behavior is involved?
A bee finds food and returns to its hive. The return-to-home ability is which behavior?
When a predator repeatedly sees a defended prey and avoids its pattern, what has the predator acquired?
An individual's own offspring count chiefly contributes to which fitness component?
Benefits gained by helping relatives reproduce contribute to which fitness component?
